topics.title: Equations of Lines
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: form linear equations with given points. (k, s)
draw the graph of a line given its equation. (u, s)

body.text: A boda boda rider in Masaka charges a fixed amount to start a trip, then the same amount for every extra kilometre. If you plot the fare against the distance, the points lie on a straight line. In this topic you learn to find the equation of a straight line from points on it, and to draw a line when you are given its equation.

Look at the points (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 5) and (3, 7). Each time x goes up by 1, y goes up by 2. When x is 0, y is 1. So each y-value is double the x-value, plus 1. We write this rule as an equation: y = 2x + 1. Every point on the line fits this equation, and every point that fits the equation lies on the line.
Any straight line that is not vertical can be written in the form y = mx + c. The two numbers m and c tell you everything about the line.

body.speech: y equals m x plus c

items: m is the gradient. The gradient measures how steep the line is. It tells you how much y changes when x increases by 1.
c is the y-intercept. This is the y-value where the line crosses the y-axis, where x = 0.
If m is positive, the line slopes upwards from left to right. If m is negative, it slopes downwards.
Lines with the same gradient are parallel. A bigger gradient gives a steeper line.

body.text: To find the gradient from two points, divide the change in y by the change in x.

body.speech: m equals y 2 minus y 1, over x 2 minus x 1

items: A horizontal line has gradient 0. Its equation is y = b, for example y = 3. Every point on it has y-coordinate 3.
A vertical line has the equation x = a, for example x = −2. Every point on it has x-coordinate −2.
The line y = x passes through (0, 0), (1, 1) and (2, 2).
The line y = −x passes through (0, 0), (1, −1) and (−2, 2).

body.text: Forming the equation from two points

body.title: The line through (1, 3) and (3, 7)
steps: Find the gradient: m = (7 − 3) ÷ (3 − 1) = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.
So the equation is y = 2x + c. We still need c.
Substitute one of the points. Using (1, 3): 3 = 2 × 1 + c, so 3 = 2 + c.
Subtract 2 from both sides: c = 1.
The equation is y = 2x + 1.
Check with the other point: 2 × 3 + 1 = 7. It fits.

body.title: A line with a negative gradient
steps: Find the equation of the line through (0, 5) and (2, 1).
The point (0, 5) is on the y-axis, so the y-intercept is c = 5.
The equation is y = −2x + 5.
Check with (2, 1): −2 × 2 + 5 = −4 + 5 = 1. It fits.

body.text: Drawing a line from its equation

To draw a line, make a table of values. Choose a few x-values, work out y for each, then plot the points and join them with a ruler. Two points are enough to fix a line, but a third point is a useful check.

body.title: Drawing y = 3x − 2
steps: Choose x-values from −1 to 3.
When x = 2, y = 4. When x = 3, y = 7.
Draw axes with x from −1 to 3 and y from −5 to 7. Choose a scale that fits your paper, such as 1 cm for 1 unit.
Plot (−1, −5), (0, −2), (1, 1), (2, 4) and (3, 7). They should lie in a straight line.
Join them with a ruler and label the line y = 3x − 2. It crosses the y-axis at −2, as c tells us.

body.title: Boda boda fares
steps: Opio charges UGX 2,000 to start a trip and UGX 1,000 for each kilometre. The fare in shillings is F = 1000d + 2000, where d is the distance in kilometres.
Table: d = 0 gives F = 2,000; d = 1 gives 3,000; d = 2 gives 4,000; d = 3 gives 5,000; d = 4 gives 6,000; d = 5 gives 7,000.
Plot distance on the horizontal axis and fare on the vertical axis, then join the points.
The gradient, 1,000, is the cost of each extra kilometre. The intercept, 2,000, is the starting charge.
Read the graph at d = 3.5. The fare is UGX 5,500. Check: 1000 × 3.5 + 2000 = 5,500.

body.title: Four in a line
body.text: In pairs, draw a coordinate grid from −5 to 5 on both axes. Take turns to plot points, each player using a different colour. The first to get four points in a straight line wins the round. Record the coordinates of each winning line and work out its equation. Then use the simulation to try different values of m and c and watch how the line moves.
How many different straight lines pass through the point (1, 1)? Write down the equations of some of them. What do all their equations have in common?

A straight line has an equation y = mx + c, where m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept. Find m by dividing the change in y by the change in x, then substitute a point to find c. To draw a line, make a table of values, plot at least three points and join them with a ruler.
